department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

deadline.value: December 15 priority deadline for fee waiver and PhD application review.
deadline.quote: PhD applications must be submitted by Dec. 15, 2026

gre_subject.value: ETS offers no subject test in this discipline.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Pre-application supervisor contact not specified as mandatory.

funding.value: PhD students are usually supported via teaching and/or research assistantships (stipend plus tuition and selected fee waiver); fellowships and waivers are also available.
funding.quote: There are several different forms of financial aid available to incoming doctoral graduate students: fellowships, teaching assistantships, research assistantships, and tuition and fee waivers. | Students in the PhD program are usually supported in the form of a teaching and/or research assistantship. Assistantship contracts are awarded on a semester basis: fall and spring, and include a stipend plus waiver of tuition and selected fees.

entry_route.value: Applicants typically hold an MS degree, though outstanding applicants with only a bachelor's degree are considered via direct admission.
entry_route.quote: Successful applicants for doctoral study should have a master of science degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, engineering physics, computer science, or a related field and should have completed substantial coursework in the chosen field of study. The department does consider outstanding PhD applicants who have only a bachelor’s degree through a program called “direct admission.”
